a: The Great Wall of China is not visible from space with the naked eye, despite a persistent myth that it is. This myth was popularized before the space age and has been repeatedly debunked by astronauts. The Great Wall is actually quite narrow, typically 5-7 meters wide, and is made of materials that blend in with the surrounding landscape. From low Earth orbit (about 400 km up), it is no more visible than countless other human-made structures like highways, airport runways, or canals. Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei confirmed after his 2003 mission that he could not see the Great Wall from space. The myth likely originated from a 1932 statement in a popular American publication (Ripley's Believe It or Not) that claimed the wall was the only man-made structure visible from the moon, which is even more false - from the moon, even continents are barely visible. What IS visible from space are larger scale human impacts: cities at night, major highways, agricultural patterns, and deforestation boundaries. The Great Wall can, however, be seen in satellite imagery (like Google Earth) because satellites can image objects down to about 0.5 meter resolution.
